title: Chicken Burrito
subtitle: Spiced chicken, rice, and black beans in a large flour tortilla
excerpt: Shredded spiced chicken layered with cumin rice, black beans, cheese, and soured cream in a large flour tortilla. Faster than the beef version and just as filling.
sourceNotes: Chicken burritos: a Tex-Mex staple based on the flour tortilla burrito tradition of northern Mexico and the US Southwest. Drawn from classic American Tex-Mex home-cooking sources.

recipe.freezeNotes: Wrap assembled burritos in foil and freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat from frozen in the oven at 180°C for 20-25 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the chicken and rice filling and freeze assembled burritos.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The chicken and rice can be made a day ahead and reheated.

content.text: A chicken burrito is a large flour tortilla wrapped around shredded spiced chicken, cumin-scented rice, and black beans, with cheese and soured cream to finish. The chicken thighs cook in under 20 minutes, rest for 5, and shred easily with two forks. Everything goes in together at the table and the tortilla is rolled tight.
Large flour tortillas at least 30 cm wide are the right size. Anything smaller and the fillings don't fit without the wrap splitting.

Put {{long-grain-rice}} of rice in a saucepan with {{stock-chicken}} of stock and the cumin. Bring to a boil, cover, reduce to the lowest heat, and cook for 12 minutes. Remove from heat; leave covered for 5 minutes.

Mix the cumin, smoked paprika, chilli powder, olive oil, and salt. Toss the chicken thighs through the mixture. Heat a frying pan over medium-high heat and cook the thighs for 6-7 minutes on each side. Rest 5 minutes, then shred with two forks. Squeeze the lime juice over the shredded chicken and toss.

Warm each flour tortilla in a dry pan for 30 seconds per side. Lay flat and place a portion of rice on the lower third, then shredded chicken, then black beans, cheese, soured cream, avocado if using, and coriander.
Fold the bottom edge up over the filling, fold the sides in, then roll up tightly from the bottom. Eat straight away.

items.cause: Tortilla not warm enough, or overfilled
items.fix: Warm the tortilla until flexible before filling. Use a medium amount of filling; the tortilla should close comfortably.

items.symptom: Chicken tastes dry inside the burrito
items.cause: Thighs overcooked, or no moisture added when shredding
items.fix: Cook thighs to just done (6-7 minutes per side) and rest before shredding. A squeeze of lime juice after shredding adds moisture and flavour.

items.symptom: Rice sticks to the pan or burns
items.cause: Heat too high, or lid lifted during steaming
items.fix: Use the lowest hob setting once covered. Don't lift the lid until the 5-minute steam is complete.

items.cause: Soured cream placed directly on the tortilla, or beans not drained
items.fix: Drain beans thoroughly before adding. Layer soured cream on top of the dry filling (rice and chicken at the base) so it doesn't soak the tortilla.

content.text: Chicken burritos follow the same format as beef: rice, beans, and protein wrapped in a large flour tortilla. Large flour tortillas come from northern Mexico. The chicken version spread through US Tex-Mex restaurant chains in the 1970s and 1980s. It is now one of the most widely made burritos in home kitchens around the world.
